data.title: MiVana Launches Organic Coffee Cherry 'Shot Drink' to Tap Into Wellness Market
data.description: MiVana Company Limited, part of the Premier Group, has launched MiVana SHOT DRINK, a ready-to-drink wellness beverage made from organic coffee cherry pulp sourced from watershed forests in the northern province of Chiang Rai. The launch expands the company’s business beyond organic coffee into the wellness market, with a sales target of 100 million baht in the first 12 months .

data.title: Bangkok Central Kitchen brings healthy meals to 150,000 students
data.description: "Bangkok, City for Better Health" launched a "Central Kitchen" at Wat Don School, enabling the preparation of nutritious meals for almost 1,500 students across seven schools in the Sathon and Bang Rak districts.

data.title: Leaders visit Pacific's Tuvalu on frontline of climate change
data.description: FUNAFUTI (TUVALU) - More than a dozen leaders visited the tiny Pacific nation of Tuvalu on Tuesday for a brief look at a once-vibrant ecosystem wiped out due to climate change.

data.title: South Korea warns of possible AI use in banking hacks
data.description: SEOUL — Artificial intelligence (AI) may have been used in a string of cyberattacks targeting South Korea's financial sector, the president said Tuesday, as police announced the launch of an investigation.

data.title: End of an era as Messi prepares to hang up Argentina boots
data.description: BUENOS AIRES - Lionel Messi will pull on Argentina's sky blue-and-white jersey for the last time on Tuesday and enjoy an emotional farewell in front of his adoring fans in a stadium with a name to match his legacy: Monumental.

data.title: Purple reign: Philippines seeks to keep grip on ube throne
data.description: PADRE GARCIA — The Philippine ube has become a trend-setting sensation from Los Angeles (LA) to London to Seoul, with the humble yam's bright purple hue drawing lines outside coffee shops and bakeries and millions of views on social media.

data.title: Myanmar leader to visit Malaysia after migrant returns begin
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR — Myanmar's coup leader turned president Min Aung Hlaing will visit Malaysia "in the next few days", Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Tuesday, after Kuala Lumpur launched a plan to return thousands of Myanmar migrants.

data.title: Central Plains floods easing, risk moving South
data.description: Floods contiue to dominate parts of Bangkok and 27 provinces, mostly in the Central Plains, but the risk is moving southwards with the approach of the annual northeast monsoon.

data.title: China Eastern reports passenger to police over cabin crew kneeling row
data.description: China Eastern Airlines has reported a male passenger to the police for allegedly disturbing order, after a flight attendant was filmed kneeling in a cabin aisle to apologise for bumping his elbow with a service trolley.

data.title: Upper House's First Residences Open for Private Viewing
data.description: The first Upper House Residences are now available to view by private appointment at the Upper House Residences Lounge on Wireless Road, Bangkok.

data.title: Conned workers still waiting for refunds after hoax recruiter jailed
data.description: BURI RAM - Representatives of about 200 workers tricked into paying a recruiter for non-existent jobs in Australia on Tuesday complained to police they were still waiting to be repaid more than a year after the woman was sent to prison and ordered to refund their money.

data.title: Seoul weighs steps to force North Korea landmine apology
data.description: SEOUL — South Korea is considering measures to force an apology from North Korea over a recent landmine blast that injured three soldiers inside the Demiltarised Zone (DMZ), its defence ministry said Tuesday.

data.title: Infrastructure projects diversify Phuket’s economy beyond tourism
data.description: Savills records 4,166 homes launched in Phuket in the first half of 2026, with villas accounting for over 61% of new housing project value.

data.title: Old woman alleges she was forcibly confined for 2 years
data.description: An elderly woman has accused her son and daughter-in-law of tricking her into entering a care centre more than two years again and kept her there against her will so they could take control of a business worth billions of baht.

data.title: Ready, set, snooze: Sleep-deprived Japanese compete for best-rested
data.description: TOKYO — In diligent, exhausted Japan, self-described elite "competitive sleepers" vied to lie down, relax and nap the fastest and deepest in a contest organised by a mattress company.

data.title: Joe Louis Theatre launches book on 125 years of Thai puppetry on Sept 24
data.description: Copies of a new Thai puppetry book are going to libraries, with an English edition planned and interactive upgrades for the completed e-book.

data.title: COP31 eyes modest steps as climate disasters multiply
data.description: PARIS - Nations reeling from a year of climate devastation gather for COP31 next month but negotiations are not expected to deliver major progress in cutting the fossil fuels driving the crisis.

data.title: IRPC joins force with PTT to provide flood relief supports
data.description: IRPC Public Company Limited (IRPC) led by Sirimeth Leepagorn, Chief Executive Officer and President, in collaboration with PTT Group, handed over relief assistance through the Ministry of Energy to alleviate the suffering of flood victims. The donation was received by Akanat Promphan, Minister of Energy; Chantanon Wannakejohn, Permanent Secretary for Energy; and Sarawut Kaewtathip, Director-General of the Department of Energy Business.

data.title: Tens of thousands expected in Paris for high school protests
data.description: PARIS — Tens of thousands of demonstrators are expected on the streets of Paris on Tuesday as France's powerful trade unions join high school students rallying for better conditions in a wave of protests marked by clashes with police.

data.title: American Nobel laureate in medicine hopes to illuminate the brain
data.description: WASHINGTON - Nobel Prize-winning American researcher Karl Deisseroth is a psychiatrist, neuroscientist and bioengineer who has spent more than two decades illuminating the workings of the brain to unlock its mysteries.

data.title: NHL record-breaker Ovechkin says current season will be his last
data.description: WASHINGTON — NHL all-time scoring leader Alex Ovechkin said Monday that the current season will be his last in the North American ice hockey league.

data.title: Islamic finance forum to chart course towards a more sustainable future
data.description: Islamic finance leaders and experts from around the world to exchange perspectives on strengthening economic resilience, mobilising transition finance, and expanding opportunities for international collaboration. The international forum, “Islamic Finance: From Crisis Resilience to Transition Finance”, will be held as an Affiliated Programme in conjunction with the 2026 Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group, hosted by Thailand. The event is scheduled for Wednesday, Oct 14, at the Grand Ballroom, The Westin Grande Sukhumvit, Bangkok.

data.title: Thailand says risk from suspected pneumonic plague case in Russia remains low
data.description: Thailand’s DDC says the risk of importing plague from a suspected case in Russia remains low, with no confirmed spread or need for extra border screening.

data.title: Sea and OpenAI Bring Regional Codex Hackathon Series to Thailand
data.description: Bangkok - Global technology company Sea and OpenAI are bringing the Sea x OpenAI Regional Codex Hackathon Series to Thailand, with the one-day hackathon taking place in Bangkok on 21 November 2026.

data.title: France roar back in Nations League as Italy beat Turkey
data.description: PARIS - Michael Olise starred as France stormed back from behind to thrash Belgium 4-1 in the Uefa Nations League on Monday, while Italy continued their resurgence with victory over Turkey.

data.title: Trump approves firing squad for convicted US military base shooter
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - President Donald Trump has approved the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist who shot dead 13 people at a military base in 2009, the Pentagon said on Monday.

data.title: Grappling with 'homework scams,' US universities shun AI detectors
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Locked in a cat-and-mouse struggle, biology professor Timothy Paustian devised novel ways to catch students turning in chatbot-generated assignments. But like many US universities, his institution is shunning AI detection software.

data.title: Thai Galleries Association stages  new international art fair in Paragon
data.description: The Thai Galleries Association is holding "Art Bangkok 2026 - The First Chapter", a new international art fair to connect Thailand's art scene with the international art world. It will kick off tomorrow and run daily from noon to 7pm until Sunday at NEX Hall and Jewel Zone, 5th floor of Siam Paragon, Rama I Road.
